# Cricket Score Counter

> Free web app for live cricket scoring, team management, player statistics, and tournament organization for local matches.

Cricket Score Counter helps cricket players, scorers, and tournament organizers score matches ball-by-ball, track batting and bowling statistics, manage local tournaments, save match history, and share live scorecards with friends and family.

## Docs

- [How It Works](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/how-it-works): Overview of how live scoring works.
- [Cricket Scoring Guide](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/cricket-scoring-guide): Guide to scoring runs, wickets, and extras.
- [Scorekeeping Tips](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/scorekeeping-tips): Practical tips for accurate live scoring.
- [Cricket Rules Guide](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/cricket-rules-guide): Reference for common cricket rules.
- [FAQ](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/faq): Frequently asked questions about the app.

## Learn Cricket

- [Learn Cricket hub](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn): All in-depth guides.
- [Cricket Glossary](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/cricket-glossary): 150+ cricket terms explained.
- [Cricket Calculators](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/cricket-calculators): Run rate, NRR, strike rate, economy, overs and rain targets.
- [The LBW Rule Explained Simply: Pitching, Impact and Shots](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/lbw-rule-explained): A plain-English guide to LBW under Law 36: where the ball pitched, where it hit the pad, whether a shot was offered, and how umpires decide without DRS.
- [Which Dismissals Count for the Bowler? Wickets Explained](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/how-wickets-are-credited): Bowled, caught, LBW, stumped and hit wicket go to the bowler. Run outs, timed out and obstruction do not. Here is how to credit every dismissal correctly.
- [Cricket Fielding Positions Explained: Slips to Long-On](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/fielding-positions-explained): Learn every cricket fielding position, from slips and gully to cover, mid-wicket and fine leg, plus the words that describe them and the leg-side rule.
- [Umpire Signals Explained: Every Signal a Scorer Must Know](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/umpire-signals-explained): A scorer's guide to cricket umpire signals: four, six, wide, no-ball, bye, leg bye, dead ball, short run, penalty runs, revoke and more, with recording tips.
- [Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) Method Explained Simply](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/duckworth-lewis-stern-explained): How the DLS method sets revised targets in rain-hit matches: resources, overs and wickets, par scores and why local cricket usually needs a simpler method.
- [Dead Ball, Short Runs and Penalty Runs Explained](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/dead-ball-and-short-runs): When is the ball dead? What counts as a short run? Who gets five penalty runs and how are they scored? A practical guide to Laws 18, 20 and 41 for scorers.
- [Ties, Super Overs and Bowl-Outs: Deciding Tied Matches](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/super-over-and-tie-rules): What counts as a tie, how a Super Over works under ICC playing conditions, what happens if the Super Over is tied, and fair tie-breakers for local cricket.
- [How to Organise a Local Cricket Match: Complete Checklist](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/how-to-organise-a-local-cricket-match): A practical checklist for organising a weekend local cricket match: booking the ground, confirming players, kit, rule sheets, timings and avoiding disputes.
- [Box Cricket Rules: Pitch, Overs, Nets and Scoring](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/box-cricket-rules): Common box cricket rules explained: team sizes, overs, pitch length, how runs are scored off the nets, dismissals and a ready-to-use 8-over rule sheet.
- [Tennis Ball and Tape Ball Cricket Rules Explained](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/tennis-ball-cricket-rules): Tennis ball and tape ball cricket rules: ball types, bowling actions, wides, no LBW, field restrictions and a sample 10-over rule sheet for weekend games.
- [Gully Cricket Rules and the House Rules Everyone Argues About](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/gully-cricket-rules): Gully and street cricket rules explained: one-tip-one-hand, last man batting, hitting into houses, trial balls, the one-pitch catch and how to settle disputes.
- [The Toss in Cricket: How It Works and Whether to Bat First](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/toss-bat-or-bowl-first): How the cricket toss works under the Laws, and how local captains should decide to bat or bowl first based on pitch, weather, light, team strength and format.
- [How to Pick Fair Teams for a Friendly Cricket Match](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/picking-fair-teams): Practical methods for picking fair teams in friendly cricket: captain's draft, skill tiers, balancing bowlers and keepers, and setting a sensible batting order.
- [Cricket Equipment Guide: Bat Sizes, Balls and Safety Gear](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/cricket-equipment-guide): Cricket equipment for local players: bat size by height, English vs Kashmir willow, ball types and weights, and the safety gear hard-ball cricket needs.
- [How to Score a Wide: Runs, Dismissals and Local Rules](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/how-to-score-wides): Learn exactly how to score a wide in cricket: the penalty run, runs taken off a wide, wides to the boundary, stumpings off a wide and common local rules.
- [No-Balls and Free Hits: How to Score Them Correctly](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/no-ball-and-free-hit-scoring): How to score a no-ball and a free hit: the penalty run, runs off the bat, byes off a no-ball, which dismissals are allowed and common local scoring errors.
- [Byes vs Leg Byes: The Difference and How to Record Them](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/byes-and-leg-byes-explained): Byes and leg byes explained for scorers: when each applies, when leg byes are not allowed, why neither counts against the bowler, with worked examples.
- [How to Record a Run Out: Runs, Batter Out and Who Faces](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/how-to-record-a-run-out): Scoring a run out properly: which runs count, how to tell which batter is out, who faces the next ball, and run outs off wides, no-balls and the last ball.
- [Overthrows in Cricket: How Boundary Overthrow Runs Count](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/overthrows-in-cricket): How overthrows are scored: extra runs from a wild throw, the boundary overthrow rule, why crossing at the instant of the throw matters, plus local rules.
- [Who Faces Next? Strike Rotation After Runs, Extras and Wickets](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/strike-rotation-explained): A scorer's guide to strike rotation: who is on strike after odd and even runs, overs, wides, no-balls, short runs and every kind of wicket, including catches.
- [How to Read a Cricket Scorecard: Batting, Bowling and FoW](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/how-to-read-a-cricket-scorecard): Learn to read any cricket scorecard: batting columns, dismissal notation, the extras line, fall of wickets and bowling figures like 4-0-28-2, with an example.
- [Net Run Rate Explained with Worked Examples](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/net-run-rate-explained): Learn how net run rate is calculated, why an all-out team counts its full quota of overs, and how to convert 18.4 overs correctly, with worked examples.
- [Chasing a Target: Planning an Innings with Required Run Rate](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/chasing-a-target-required-run-rate): How to use required run rate to plan a run chase: calculating it correctly, breaking the target into phases, and when to attack or consolidate in local cricket.
- [Rain-Shortened Matches: Setting Fair Revised Targets](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/shortened-match-targets): Simple, fair ways to set revised targets when rain shortens a local cricket match, with worked examples, honest weaknesses, and how DLS works in principle.
- [Powerplay Strategy for Batting and Bowling Sides](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/powerplay-strategy): Powerplay rules for T20 and ODI cricket, how to scale them for local formats, and practical batting, bowling and field-setting plans for the opening overs.
- [Death Overs Bowling: Yorkers, Slower Balls and Fields](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/death-overs-bowling-tips): Death overs bowling tips for club cricketers: yorkers, slower balls, wide yorkers, field settings and over-by-over plans, with a worked final-overs example.
- [Batting Tips for Beginners: Grip, Stance and Defence](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/batting-tips-for-beginners): Batting tips for new cricketers: how to grip the bat, set a balanced stance, play forward and back defence, leave the ball and rotate the strike in matches.
- [Bowling Tips for Beginners: Run-Up, Action and Length](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/learn/bowling-tips-for-beginners): Beginner bowling tips covering grip, a repeatable run-up, a legal and safe action, front-foot no-balls, and how to find a good line and length in matches.

## App

- [Create a Game](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/create-game): Start scoring a new match, no account required.
- [Join a Game](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/join-game): Follow a live match via a shared link.
- [Download the Android App](https://www.cricket-score-counter.com/download-app): Get the native Android app.
